papers.title: LLM-Based Feature Extraction for Multi-Criteria Inventory Classification
papers.abstract: E-commerce supply chains generate large volumes of customer feedback and operational data that remain underutilized in inventory management. Traditional inventory classification techniques such as ABC analysis rely primarily on annual dollar usage, while multi-criteria inventory classification (MCIC) methods extend this but still depend on structured quantitative data and do not utilize unstructured information available in modern supply chains. This paper proposes an LLM-based feature extraction approach that transforms unstructured sources such as customer reviews into quantitative features using vector embeddings and LLM-generated evaluation criteria. The enriched feature set is incorporated into an MCIC framework based on the Hadi-Vencheh model. Experimental results show measurable reclassification effects when customer sentiment signals are included, demonstrating that integrating unstructured data into MCIC can enhance inventory prioritization.

papers.title: On Seeding Watermarks to Detect Verbatim LLM Copy-Paste Responses
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have made fluent essay writing, code drafting, and quiz answering instantly available to students at every level, from secondary school through graduate study. Many educators do not object to LLM use \emph{per~se}; what they need to detect is the case in which a student pastes the assignment prompt into a chatbot and submits the model's reply verbatim, without engaging with the work. Existing post-hoc AI-text detectors remain unreliable and have been shown to penalise non-native English writers, while output-side watermarks require cooperation from the model provider. We propose an alternative that the educator controls directly: an input-side watermark in which an invisible instruction is embedded inside the visible assignment prompt itself. An LLM that ingests the prompt verbatim quietly reads the hidden instruction and writes a tell-tale signature into its reply, exposing the copy-and-paste pathway specifically. We describe SteganoPrompt, a single-page, zero-dependency web tool that encodes an arbitrary printable-ASCII payload into the deprecated Unicode Tags block (\texttt{U+E0000}--\texttt{U+E007F}). The encoded string is visually identical to the original, survives common copy-paste channels (Word, Google Docs, PDF, Markdown, Slack, e-mail, the major learning-management systems), and is tokenized as ordinary text by most frontier models. We evaluate compliance across eight LLM families and a representative set of educational content channels. To keep deployment transparent, disclosure is built into the tool itself: every encoded brief also carries a brief, always-on academic-integrity reminder for the student, and we set out concrete guidance recommending for its disclosed, ethical use in the classroom. The tool is released under the MIT licence at https://ezharjan.github.io/SteganoPrompt/.

papers.title: Circuit Theory-Informed AI for Condition Monitoring in Power Electronics
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence for power electronics is evolving toward a deeper comprehension of system intrinsic behaviors and dynamics. As a novel integration of neural computation and electric circuits, spike-based neuromorphic computing offers promising potential in high energy efficiency and adaptability for data-driven applications. Building on the latency-coding principles, this article proposes a framework for data-light condition monitoring that relies solely on three-phase AC current measurements. The AC current signals are encoded as membrane potentials of RC-based spiking neurons, which are inherently compatible with spiking neural networks that can effectively facilitate the estimation of device parameters. Case studies are presented to validate the performances, while constraints and further optimizations are also evaluated and discussed, and future extensions of the methodology are provided.

papers.title: StreamAZ: Line-by-Line SAR Focusing with State Space Models
papers.abstract: Conventional focusing methods for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) employ block-wise processing efficiently but remain latency-heavy processes that prevent the realisation of a closed-loop cognitive SAR system. We present an online SAR image-formation framework, StreamAZ, that treats sensing as a stream and produces focused images in a line by line fashion. Our method uses a tiny state-space surrogate model trained with teacher-student distillation and multi-stage losses. We evaluate the method on real SAR data from Maya4, a Sentinel-1-derived dataset containing raw, range-compressed, range-cell-migration-corrected, and azimuth-compressed products. Relative to a linewise digital-signal-processing baseline, our framework delivers approximately 70$\times$ lower latency and 130$\times$ lower memory use; on a single AMD CPU core it processes one row in 16 ms with a memory footprint of 6 MB whilst maintaining a focusing quality high enough to support downstream decisions, which we illustrate with vessel detection and flood-mapping tasks.

papers.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Annealing for Protein Side-Chain Optimization: A Feasibility Study
papers.abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical annealing solvers are moving from research laboratories toward industrial use, but their advantage over classical optimization appears to be confined to a narrow class of problems. A recent systematic benchmark of the D-Wave hybrid solver against industry-leading classical solvers, across several classes of optimization problems, found it to be most competitive on binary quadratic programs, while noting that few industrial problems take this form. Therefore, identifying real-world industrial problems that can be modeled with this structure is a key challenge. We propose protein side-chain optimization, a core step of computational protein design, as one of these problems: it is natively a binary quadratic program, and its application context requires pools of low-energy solutions, which annealers naturally return. In this feasibility study, we test whether the competitiveness of the hybrid solver against industry-leading classical solvers extends to this problem. On 40 instances derived from 20 experimentally determined protein structures with up to about 200 amino acids and 2000 binary variables, we compare the results achieved with a hybrid solver, run for 5 seconds, against those of the commercial solver Gurobi, run for 10 seconds, 1000 seconds, and 4 hours. The hybrid solver reaches the certified optimum whenever one is available, matches Gurobi's performance on smaller instances, and outperforms it on larger instances, finding lower-energy solutions. These results show that the competitiveness of the hybrid solver on binary quadratic programs, so far observed only on a synthetic benchmark, extends to a real-world problem. This motivates comparisons with classical heuristics specific to protein side-chain optimization.

papers.title: Efficient Spintronic Stochastic In-Sensor Computing Modules
papers.abstract: In-sensor processing (ISP) is used in various fields, including autonomous driving automotive systems, wearable healthcare devices, environmental monitoring, wireless sensor networks, smart cities, and industrial control systems. One of the main features of most of these applications is energy and hardware restriction. This restriction amplifies the importance of using high-performance and low-energy consumption computing systems and methods. This paper proposes efficient spintronic stochastic computing modules for in-sensor computing systems to address this challenge. The proposed design utilized the stochastic behavior of the magnetic tunnel junction in the subcritical switching regime to generate a probability-adjustable random stream. Probability-adjustable random stream generation is the most important step in any stochastic system because it determines the quality of the final output. The simulation results indicate that the proposed design offers almost the same peak signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity while occupying at least 62\% lower area and consuming 60\% lower energy. These advantages made the proposed design a good choice for ISP applications with limited energy.

papers.title: SEU Hardened Multi-Context Spintronic FPGA
papers.abstract: Due to susceptibility to radiation-induced soft errors and resource constraints implementing large and complex designs on field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) in harsh environments is challenging. Therefore, to mitigate these issues, this paper proposes an innovative approach through the introduction of a single event upset (SEU)-hardened spintronic FPGA architecture that incorporates multi-context capabilities. Leveraging the non-volatile properties of magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ), the proposed design can store two/four distinct configurations internally, eliminating the dependence on external non-volatile memory which significantly boosts the system performance. Additionally, through post-layout simulation, we demonstrate our design immunity to SEU, which enhances its reliability and operational stability in environments susceptible to radiation-induced soft errors. The efficiency of the proposed design was also evaluated using the ROSSETA benchmark, which serves as a representative model for real-world FPGA applications.

papers.title: Investigating Anthropometric Fidelity in SAM 3D Body
papers.abstract: The release of SAM 3D Body is a recent development in human mesh recovery, demonstrating improved performance in producing clean, topologically coherent meshes from single images. By leveraging the Momentum Human Rig (MHR), it achieves robustness to occlusion and diverse poses. However, our evaluation reveals a specific and consistent limitation: the model struggles to reconstruct detailed anthropometric deviations, particularly in populations exhibiting distinctive morphological alterations such as geriatric muscle atrophy, scoliosis, or pregnancy, even when these features are prominent in the input image. In this paper, we investigate this phenomenon not as a failure of the model's capacity, but as a byproduct of the "perception-distortion trade-off". We posit that the architectural reliance on the low-dimensional parametric MHR representation, combined with semantic-invariant conditioning (DINOv3) and annotation-based alignment, creates a pervasive "regression to the mean" effect. We analyze these mechanisms to understand why individual biological details are smoothed out. Furthermore, we state our contributions by proposing specific, constructive pathways for future work, such as implicit-explicit hybrid representations and Medical-in-the-Loop alignment, to extend the baseline performance of SAM 3D Body into the high-precision medical domain.

papers.title: Quantum Integration Software Suite For HPC-Quantum Computing Workflows
papers.abstract: In this work, we focus on addressing challenges related to modelling the integration of conventional high-performance computing (HPC) and quantum computing (QC). We introduce the Quantum Assembly Compiler (QASC) for OpenQASM3.0 files. The compiler produces an executable that leverages the high-performance simulator QuEST to simulate quantum programs. Additionally, we introduce a performance modelling tool, QACC-perf, which can estimate the cost of integrating QC in classical HPC workflows, as well as the execution time of the quantum circuits. Finally, we demonstrate the utility of these tools in the context of multiscale quantum chemistry workflows using the ChemShell computational chemistry environment.
